source: Authenticated status SSE subscriptions, retained JSONL history, and live run events.
control: A bounded event broker enforces global, per-principal, and per-run subscriber quotas, bounded per-consumer queues, one-time replay, backpressure deadlines, sequence-gap failure, retention, and disconnect cleanup without polling storage.
sink: Control Center SSE response writers, Node.js event-loop capacity, and status-event storage reads.
boundary: Authenticated principals may open streams, but no principal or run may allocate unbounded subscribers, queued bytes, or repeated full-history parsing.

pre_fix_negative.result: Exact pre-fix polling and full-file replay functions amplified history reads across concurrent clients and ignored response backpressure.

source: Append-only status-event JSONL files, including histories with large or malformed prefixes and records.

boundary: An authorized caller may request recent events, but historical file size and attacker-shaped earlier records cannot force a full-file read.

source: Hosted project metadata selected through the verified workload pointer and lock.
control: An explicit required-or-optional runtime mode replaces NODE_ENV trust inference; canonical Compose selects required, missing locks fail closed, and required mode accepts metadata only when its path, size, and digest record are bound to the verified lock. Metadata remains pre-bounded and parsed in an interruptible worker.
sink: Project Router discovery, cache entries, and upstream routing decisions.
boundary: A hosted workload author may shape metadata, but required runtime mode cannot consume an absent lock, unsigned record, unbounded input, or metadata outside the verified lock generation.

pre_fix_negative.result: Bounded synthetic oversized, deep, high-alias, and repeatedly changing files reached the exact pre-fix unbounded read/parse path; QA replay also showed missing-lock and unsigned-record acceptance without an explicit mode.

tests.aggregate: Project Router focused suite: 7/7 passing. All local Node tests: 128/128 passing; shell syntax checks: 111/111 passing.

independent_qa.local_evidence: Focused router and full aggregate suites passed after QA remediation on the cohort branch.
independent_qa.required: Replay missing lock, missing record, unsigned metadata, and explicit Compose runtime-mode probes after patch-equivalent cherry-pick.

runtime_status.evidence: Worker deadlines, cache binding, lock absence, unsigned records, and pointer tampering were exercised with disposable fixtures; no live hosted workload or router listener was used.

external_conditions: Hosted deployment must prepare and atomically publish the verified workload lock and pointer with the expected private ownership and permissions.

rollback.safety: Revert newest support first, then earlier support and cohort; disable hosted metadata routing unless equivalent parse budgets, explicit required mode, and verified-lock binding remain.

source: Read-only hosted project directory trees whose depth, width, file sizes, symlinks, namespace entries, and filesystem latency may be workload-shaped.
control: Disk accounting uses a hard-deadline worker, explicit queue and unique-inflight limits, and Linux descriptor-anchored traversal. The trusted project-root descriptor is opened O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW; descendants are opened relative to /proc/self/fd parent descriptors with O_NOFOLLOW and never by original pathname. Unsupported platforms fail closed. Depth, node, byte, concurrency, cache, stale-data, and cooperative time ceilings remain.
sink: Control Center context construction, filesystem operations, worker capacity, file descriptors, and Node.js event-loop availability.
boundary: A hosted workload author may shape or rename the mounted tree while an authenticated viewer triggers context construction; namespace swaps cannot redirect an opened generation, and queued, active, and unique scans must all settle within bounded resources.

pre_fix_negative.result: The exact pre-fix synchronous walker exhausted disposable wide, deep, symlinked, and slow trees; QA replay additionally showed no hard deadline, unbounded queue/inflight state, and pathname reopen after a parent namespace swap.

tests.aggregate: Project disk focused suite: 8/8 passing; Control Center package: 55/55 passing. All local Node tests: 128/128 passing; shell syntax checks: 111/111 passing.

independent_qa.local_evidence: Portable descriptor-generation, deadline, queue, fallback, Control Center, and full aggregate suites passed after QA remediation.
independent_qa.required: Replay the parent rename/symlink PoC and /proc/self/fd traversal on Ubuntu/Linux after patch-equivalent cherry-pick; measure representative mount latency and concurrency.

runtime_status.evidence: Disposable trees and an in-memory opened-generation swap passed on macOS; non-Linux production fallback returned descriptor-unavailable. Linux /proc/self/fd execution was not run because Docker/Linux runtime was excluded.

external_conditions: Ubuntu/Linux must expose /proc/self/fd with ordinary container descriptor semantics; production tree scale, mount latency, and acceptable stale-data thresholds require operational calibration.

rollback.safety: Revert newest support before the cohort only with project disk accounting disabled or replaced by a hard-deadline, pending-work-bounded, descriptor-safe source.
